text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Farmers in the Mekong Delta are trying to harvest 1.4 million hectares of summer-autumn paddy crop before the arrival of seasonal flooding, expected in the next ten days.
-- The National AIDS Committee has announced that Vietnam has detected 6,469 people with the AIDS virus as of July 26.
-- Vietnam exported 410,000-420,000 tonnes of rice in July, a decrease of about 100,000 tonnes compared with June.
-- The World Bank, the Asian Development Bank and Japan will continue to be the three biggest donors to Vietnam in the coming years, according to the Planning and Investment Ministry.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi says the state economic sector should be strong and occupy a leading role as the country develops a multi-sector economy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for higher quality rice production in the southern Mekong Delta provinces.
-- More than 1.1 million hectares of paddy field has been transplanted in the northern Red River Delta.
-- The Hanoi People's Committee has outlined instructions for decorating buildings in the city ahead of November's Francophone summit.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has urged local authorities in the Mekong Delta to prepare carefully against early flooding.
